newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Russia's Lebed says Afghan situation very tense.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Lebed says Afghan situation very tense.

text.p: Russian security supremo Alexander Lebed, arriving in Brussels on Sunday on a first-ever visit to the NATO alliance, described the situation in Afghanistan as very tense.

"(The situation is) very tense. Hostilities are continuing. There is a movement towards the borders of Uzbekistan and Tajikistan, first moves towards implementing notions of joining parts of Tajikistan to Afghanistan," he told reporters on arrival at Brussels airport.
Lebed said he intended to open a "complicated but civilised dialogue" with NATO leaders over their plans to accept member states from former communist eastern Europe.
Lebed said that he had some new proposals to put to NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana but declined to give details of what these might be.
"We will evaluate the situation from the point of view of Russia's interests," he said.
Moscow opposes plans to enlarge the alliance, saying it is no longer necessary in the post-Cold War era.
